articles.summary: U.S. federal investigators pursuing the ShinyHunters hacking group that recently stole highly sensitive data from the FBI have identified executives at two different ransomware negotiation firms who maintained unusually close relations with the extortion group, KrebsOnSecurity has learned. Police also seized about 6.4 million stolen logins belonging to more than 40,000 victims, according to Germany's Federal Criminal Police Office (BKA).

Service was back by early afternoon, and most of the coverage focused on people who couldn’t write, code or research for a morning.

clusters.summary:
Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 is reporting today that it has tracked a massive China-based attack leveraging the open-source AI penetration testing framework Cairn to autonomously conduct 25 operations against at least 19 organizations. The attackers weaponized Cairn by pairing it with Chinese AI models Zhipu GLM and DeepSeek, Unit 42 said.

clusters.summary:
An active threat campaign is combining port scanning, password guessing, and Transact-SQL (T-SQL) commands to compromise exposed Microsoft SQL servers and deliver malware.
The attackers are using predefined username and password lists to brute-force into these servers and exploit their administrative capabilities to execute commands on the underlying Windows systems.

clusters.title: AI found Linux kernel bugs that remained undetected for decades
clusters.summary:
A Microsoft research project combining AI agents with human security researchers uncovered 59 Linux kernel vulnerabilities, including bugs that had survived in production code for more than 20 years.
While AI dramatically accelerated the discovery process, the researchers found that validating flaws, developing patches, and working with maintainers remained overwhelmingly human-intensive.

clusters.summary: CVE-2026-102895 is a trivial authentication-bypass vulnerability. GPUStack is also an attractive target. It is open-source software that manages clusters of GPUs, which are typically used to run AI workloads. All versions of GPUStack prior to 2.2.0, which was released at the end of June. This vulnerability was not made public until the end of July, and the CVE was assigned on November 4th.

clusters.title: The developer laptop just became production. Now what?
clusters.summary:
For decades, enterprise software development relied on an assumption that developers could experiment relatively safely because there were safeguards between their work and production. Development, staging and production had different rules, with human intermediaries making judgments about what was ready to move forward. Testing also assumed that software would behave predictably when executed again.

clusters.summary:
As AI model training and distillation increase, AI tokens are becoming a piping hot currency for threat actors.
Cloud hosting provider Railway found out the hard way; it has confirmed a near 26-hour battle against attackers targeting AI provider credentials to sell to AI ‘transfer stations’ for use in model distillation. The crooks generated about $740,000 in fraudulent AI usage charges using the stolen credentials and potentially had access to up to 100,000 workspace credentials.

clusters.summary: The CCP built a Big Data system to scrape reams of information and learn about individuals abroad, to potentially target and exploit them. Think Alice Huang Lite.

clusters.summary: It's hard to detect whether someone is using artificial intelligence (AI) to cheat on IT certification exams, but new tools and processes are emerging to boost trust.

clusters.title: Microsoft Patch Tuesday November 2026, (Tue, Nov 10th)
clusters.summary: Microsoft continues its AI-induced patch surge, addressing 1,260 different vulnerabilities this month. 68 of these vulnerabilities are considered critical. 167 of the vulnerabilities are Chromium issues affecting Microsoft Edge.

clusters.title: Who Runs the Ransomware Group Qilin?
clusters.summary: The cybercrime group Qilin has emerged as the world's most active ransomware affiliate program, claiming at least 365 victim organizations in the past three months alone. But even top Russian hackers make operational security mistakes, and the administrator of Qilin has made a few key missteps over the last decade that all point to a 36-year-old man living in St. Petersburg, Russia.

clusters.title: Rewriting less than 10 neurons in an LLM can turn it into a sleeper backdoor
clusters.summary:
Microsoft researchers have found that rewriting fewer than 10 rarely used neurons in an open-weight AI model can turn any agent built on it into a sleeper backdoor that runs an attacker’s commands on cue, with no retraining required.

clusters.summary:

clusters.title: Why does old access outlive the job?
clusters.summary: Old access persists beyond its intended purpose and most organizations never monitor it. New access rights arrive within a day of a request. Old rights get revoked, if they get revoked at all, only upon prompting someone. clusters.summary: Microsoft did another four-digit patch drop today, releasing updates to fix almost 1,100 security vulnerabilities in its Windows operating systems and supported software. This month's Patch Tuesday addresses 63 critical flaws -- including a zero-day in Microsoft Outlook -- and comes amid important security updates from other software makers, including Adobe, Apple, Google and Mozilla.

clusters.title: Want to Rent an Internet Address at the White House?
clusters.summary: Several staffers at the White House are using computers or mobile devices equipped with residential proxy services that render their internet address available for others to rent, security experts warned today. One of the proxy services is a Russian company whose founder's web hosting business was ground zero for cyberattacks against election systems in Arizona and Illinois in 2016.

clusters.title: Tech Firms Dismantle Botnet That Turned 1.3M TV Boxes Into Proxies
clusters.summary: Google said today it worked with industry partners to dismantle a botnet made up of more than 1.3 million Android TV set-top boxes that ship with malicious software which secretly rents the user's Internet connection out to strangers and conducts advertising fraud. Experts involved in the takedown say the action is likely to sever the botnet's access to more than 10 million additional compromised systems, including other Internet of Things (IoT) products such as Android-based healthcare devices

clusters.title: Widespread PHP Flaw May Cause Many Site Outages Today
clusters.summary: Expect to see quite a few websites serving "404" or "Page Not Found" errors today: Nearly 70 percent of websites need to update their core software to fix a pair of vulnerabilities that allow an attacker to seize full control over affected servers. Experts say there are working exploits for the flaws, and that these critical bugs are already being exploited in the wild.

clusters.title: Feds Suspect Ransom Negotiator Ran ShinyHunters Extortion Site
clusters.summary: U.S. federal investigators pursuing the ShinyHunters hacking group that recently stole highly sensitive data from the FBI have identified executives at two different ransomware negotiation firms who maintained unusually close relations with the extortion group, KrebsOnSecurity has learned. Sources close to the investigation say one of the executives in the United States even helped ShinyHunters operate a website that pressured victims into paying a ransom.

clusters.title: U.K. Sanctions Cryptomus for RU Money Laundering
clusters.summary: The United Kingdom has issued economic sanctions against Cryptomus, a chameleonic cryptocurrency platform that experts say serves as a major conduit for payments related to ransomware, narcotics, darknet markets, fraud and cybercrime services that are helping Russia circumvent existing financial restrictions.

clusters.title: Microsoft Patches More Than 1,400 Security Flaws
clusters.summary: Microsoft today issued updates to fix more than 1,400 security vulnerabilities in its Windows operating systems and other software. Today's epic patch batch dwarfs September's record of nearly 1,000 fixes, which was already about ten times the normal monthly patch load from Redmond.

clusters.title: FBI Arrests Executive at Ransomware Negotiation Firm
clusters.summary: Agents with the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) on Thursday arrested the co-founder of a Canadian cybersecurity firm in connection with an investigation into the ShinyHunters hacking group that recently relieved the FBI of sensitive data on thousands of agents, multiple sources tell KrebsOnSecurity.

clusters.title: ShinyHunters Extorted Boeing Spin-off Prior to Arrests
clusters.summary: A teenager from Amman, Jordan suspected of leading the prolific data theft and extortion group ShinyHunters has been detained and is reportedly cooperating with the FBI to identify other members of the hacking gang. top3.title: The firewall becomes the foothold: Attackers turn Check Point gateways against customers
top3.summary:
A firewall is intended to be a boundary attackers can’t cross.
But firewalls face the web, making them just as vulnerable to attack as other systems, as evidenced by the emergency hotfixes released by Check Point Software for several of its products.
